claim: Fascin limits Myosin activity within Drosophila border cells to control substrate stiffness and promote migration.
source: Fascin limits Myosin activity within Drosophila border cells to control substrate stiffness and promote migration
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the title and supported throughout the manuscript with experimental data including AFM measurements, pMRLC staining, and migration assays.

claim: Loss of Fascin results in increased activated Myosin on the border cells.
source: Loss of Fascin results in: increased activated Myosin on the border cells and their substrate, the nurse cells; decreased border cell Myosin dynamics; and increased nurse cell stiffness as measured by atomic force microscopy.
evidence: Supported by pMRLC staining data shown in Figure 2B', D demonstrating increased active Myosin on border cells in fascin mutants.

claim: Loss of Fascin results in increased activated Myosin on the nurse cells.
source: Loss of Fascin results in: increased activated Myosin on the border cells and their substrate, the nurse cells; decreased border cell Myosin dynamics; and increased nurse cell stiffness as measured by atomic force microscopy.
evidence: Supported by pMRLC staining data shown in Figure 2B, C demonstrating increased active Myosin on nurse cell membranes in fascin mutants.

claim: Loss of Fascin results in decreased border cell Myosin dynamics.
source: Loss of Fascin results in: increased activated Myosin on the border cells and their substrate, the nurse cells; decreased border cell Myosin dynamics; and increased nurse cell stiffness as measured by atomic force microscopy.
evidence: Supported by live imaging data showing increased MRLC-GFP puncta lifetime in fascin mutants (Figure 2H-I).

claim: Loss of Fascin results in increased nurse cell stiffness as measured by atomic force microscopy.
source: Loss of Fascin results in: increased activated Myosin on the border cells and their substrate, the nurse cells; decreased border cell Myosin dynamics; and increased nurse cell stiffness as measured by atomic force microscopy.
evidence: Supported by AFM measurements shown in Figure 3D demonstrating increased nurse cell stiffness in fascin mutants.

claim: Reducing Myosin restores on-time border cell migration in fascin mutant follicles.
source: Reducing Myosin restores on-time border cell migration in fascin mutant follicles.
evidence: Supported by migration index data in Figure 4 showing that pharmacological inhibition of Myosin or germline knockdown of MRLC rescues migration delays in fascin mutants.

claim: Fascin's actin bundling activity is required to limit Myosin activation.
source: Further, Fascin's actin bundling activity is required to limit Myosin activation.
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 5 showing that phosphomimetic Fascin (S52E), which cannot bundle actin, fails to reduce Myosin activation in fascin mutants.

claim: Fascin regulates Myosin activity in the border cells to control nurse cell stiffness to promote migration.
source: Surprisingly, we find that Fascin regulates Myosin activity in the border cells to control nurse cell stiffness to promote migration.
evidence: Supported by cell-specific knockdown and rescue experiments in Figures 6 and 7 showing that Fascin in border cells controls nurse cell stiffness.

claim: Collectively migrating cells play a critical role in controlling the mechanical properties of their substrate in order to promote their own migration.
source: Thus, these data shift the paradigm from a substrate stiffness-centric model of regulating migration, to uncover that collectively migrating cells play a critical role in controlling the mechanical properties of their substrate in order to promote their own migration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing border cells control nurse cell stiffness.

claim: This means of mechanical regulation of migration is likely conserved across contexts and organisms, as Fascin and Myosin are common regulators of cell migration.

claim: A migration index of approximately one indicates on-time migration during S9.

source: A migration index of approximately one indicates on-time migration during S9, while a value less that one indicates delayed migration and a value greater than one indicates an accelerated migration.

source: A migration index of approximately one indicates on-time migration during S9, while a value less that one indicates delayed migration and a value greater than one indicates an accelerated migration.

claim: Germline knockdown of MRLC in fascin mutant follicles rescues border cell migration.

claim: Fascin is required to limit Myosin activity within the nurse cells to promote on-time border cell migration.

claim: Phosphorylation of Fascin at serine 52 (S52, mammalian S39) inhibits its F-actin bundling function.

claim: Fascin functions in other ways besides bundling F-actin and limiting Myosin activity to promote on-time border cell migration.

source: Together our data indicate that Fascin acts in the border cells to regulate the stiffness of both the border cell cluster and its substrate, the nurse cells.

claim: The nurse cells respond to changes in stiffness of the border cells by altering their own cellular stiffness.

source: We also show that this force balance is not specific to Fascin, as directly altering Myosin activity within the border cells phenocopies knockdown of Fascin in these cells.

source: Together our data uncover that in vivo, collectively migrating cells modulate the stiffness of their substrate to control their own migration (Figure 8).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, shown in Figure 8.
